Fisher information peaks elsewhere, though, which marks a true trade-off. They also find the least entanglement that keeps a quantum edge.
arxiv-2603-13744: Shiyun Zhang and co-authors propose new research paradigms that join materials science with artificial intelligence. The classical material tetrahedron links structure, property, processing, performance, and characterization, and guides experiments, modeling, and theory. AI has soared in language and vision, yet how to merge it with natural science is still a grand challenge. The authors propose two new tetrahedra for data-driven, AI-augmented research. One, for AI in materials science, links Matter, Data, Model, Potential, and Agent. The other maps the core links of AI research itself.
arxiv-2603-13944: Jia and co-authors propose ToMPC, a task-oriented model predictive control scheme for safe robot manipulation. It unifies collision-free motion and contact interaction in one framework. Task-oriented obstacle avoidance uses the arm's spare kinematic freedom to widen the working range in clutter. The hard optimization is split by ADMM into two subproblems, solved by dynamic programming and quadratic programming. Tests in simulation and on a Franka Panda arm show real-time planning. Safety limits hold as hard constraints throughout.
arxiv-2603-14244: Vu, Le, and Phung design a tiny, cheap submarine for water quality checks, modeled on squid jet motion. Pump-driven jets move and steer the craft, and a pump system sets depth and takes water samples. Off-the-shelf parts include an ESP32 chip, motion and pressure sensors, GPS, and a LoRa radio. Total hardware cost lands near 123 dollars. Pool and lake tests show steady attitude, depth held within a tenth of a meter at 2.5 meters, and quick steering response.
arxiv-2603-14644: Pan and co-authors release LUMINA, a multi-vendor mammography benchmark with an energy harmonization step. Open breast imaging sets stay small and short on vendor range. LUMINA holds 1,824 images from 468 patients across six systems. Labels are pathology-confirmed, with BI-RADS and density notes attached. High- and low-energy image styles both appear. A foreground-only alignment maps images to a low-energy reference. Two-view models beat single-view ones on diagnosis and related tasks, they report. Harmonization lifts scores further across vendors.
arxiv-2603-15344: Garg and Cejas hunt cross-protocol anomalies in mobile core networks with a consensus of embedding models. Signaling runs over SS7, Diameter, and GTP at once, so faults may show only in the joint view. With few labeled attacks, they work unsupervised on fused per-minute records for each subscriber. Six embedding models flag records, and a consensus score counts the votes. On about 219,000 records, under one percent won full agreement. High consensus tied strongly to synthetic test anomalies, which helps analysts triage a small, rich candidate set.
arxiv-2603-15444: Proske and co-authors build a compact ultra-high vacuum cell from the glass-ceramic MACOR for cold-atom quantum technology. Field uses need small, custom, non-magnetic vacuum hardware. Their cell links to standard CF flanges and offers high-aperture viewports for precise optical work. It has held pressures below ten to the minus ten millibar for over a year. The cell already serves inside a quantum gas experiment. The team presents it as a low-cost base for wider quantum technology use.
arxiv-2603-15644: Guo and co-authors test how token design shapes health record foundation models. These models learn from long timelines of timed clinical events. The team pretrained a transformer on pediatric records under a factorial design. They varied event coding, time coding, and workflow notes. Joint event coding and positional time coding won on nearly all 74 prediction tasks. Both also cut pretraining compute, by 39.5 and 9.6 percent. A test on adult ICU data showed the joint coding gain carries over.
arxiv-2603-16044: Shin boosts a robot model's language reach with synthetic instruction variety. OpenVLA leads vision-language-action models but falters in fresh scenes. His plan enriches the Bridge Dataset V2 with reworded commands. A large language model writes varied twins of each instruction. The pairs keep meaning while shifting structure and phrasing. LoRA fine-tuning then teaches OpenVLA on the widened set. Few weights move, so training stays cheap and light. Robustness gains suggest language breadth is the key gap. Specialized datasets need richer wording, he argues.
arxiv-2603-16244: Song tests whether extra rounds of review improve checking across separate sessions. Cross-Context Review splits writing and review into independent sessions. The dynamic version lets the reviewer ask questions and review again. In a test with 30 artifacts and 150 planted errors, the single pass won. Its F1 score was 0.376, above all multi-turn variants. Extra rounds raised recall but added 62% more false alarms. Reviewers invented findings and drifted to grading the chat itself.
arxiv-2603-16444: Jillani and co-authors slim down a top hand mesh reconstruction model. Heavy models bar use on headsets and phones. Their Fast-HaMeR swaps the ViT-H backbone for lighter networks. Three distillation strategies pass knowledge from the big model. Light backbones at 35% of the size ran 1.5 times faster, with accuracy slipping by only 0.4 mm. Output-level distillation helped most students. Feature-level worked better for larger students.
arxiv-2603-16544: Piryani, Mert, and Jatowt ask how often answers to questions actually change. Language models lean on stale knowledge for time-sensitive questions. Systems need a signal for when fresh data is required. Their taxonomy sorts questions by change rate and stability. RecencyQA holds 4,031 open-domain questions with such labels. Human checks and data analysis back the labels. Questions whose recency depends on context proved hardest. Difficulty grew as update frequency rose.
arxiv-2603-16644: Garrison and Ipsen analyze normal equations solved in mixed precision. A random preconditioner is built cheaply in low precision. Several preconditioned forms are covered, from symmetric to not-normal. Their bounds are realistic and informative. Conditioning depends only mildly on preconditioner quality. It does depend on the least squares residual size. Tests show accuracy near Matlab's mldivide, with GPU-friendly speed. A fast check picks the working precision on its own.
arxiv-2603-17044: Rao and Rachuri ask whether preference tuning can align image understanding and image generation in one unified model. They apply DPO to Janus-Pro at 1B and 7B sizes, under seven training strategies. Their central finding is negative: generation quality resists DPO in every tested condition. At 7B, no method improved generation scores; at 1B, all methods degraded them. Gradient checks show the two tasks pull in near orthogonal directions, with a large size imbalance. They identify discrete VQ tokenization as a likely bottleneck.
arxiv-2603-17444: Shenderuk-Zhidkov and Hramov argue that language models now mediate between brain data and society. They call this role Neuro-Linguistic Integration. Models can aid communication, medicine, and education in that seat, they write. The same seat risks mental autonomy and fair access to meaning. Current rules like GDPR guard data, not this act of interpretation. They propose consent, transparency, and agency rules, plus a second-order neuroethics.
arxiv-2603-18144: Roettenbacher and co-authors present the first direct images of starspots on zeta And, a giant star in an RS CVn pair. The CHARA Array took the shots over three rounds and about six spins of the star. The views show a far more mixed surface than light curves and Doppler maps had hinted. Spots shift on the spin timescale, which makes spin rate gaps hard to pin down. The polar spot grows with time, and the mate star is not seen.
arxiv-2603-18244: Rubinstein-Salzedo and Zhou settle which finite sizes partisan misère quotients can take. They show every finite cardinality except 3 can occur. Allen had asked whether such sizes were restricted. The result contrasts with impartial misère quotients, which must have even cardinality. Partisan play thus allows far more quotient sizes than impartial play.
arxiv-2603-18444: Kim and co-authors propose discounted Beta-Bernoulli reward estimation for reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. Group methods estimate rewards from few rollouts, causing high variance and collapse. They recast advantage computation as estimating a reward distribution from finite samples. Historical reward statistics feed a discounted estimator with lower, stable variance despite some bias. Across nine reasoning benchmarks, GRPO with their estimator beat naive GRPO at no extra cost.
arxiv-2603-18744: Sinjan and co-authors measure and correct stray light in the Solar Orbiter PHI high resolution telescope. The craft views the Sun from as close as 0.28 astronomical units. Heat load and a wide bright field make false light a real risk. Limb profiles and a Mercury transit quantify the stray light share. A correction term joins the image reconstruction. Quiet Sun contrast rises and strong field features darken after correction. Field values then match SDO/HMI products far more closely, pixel by pixel, across most solar features.
arxiv-2603-18944: Huang and co-authors bound errors for computer schemes that solve noisy partial differential equations. They give a general proof method that holds over long times, not just early steps. It checks both the brief start phase and the long-run behavior. They study equations whose growth terms break a common smoothness rule. A classic scheme can blow up in finite time for one such case. They prove lasting error bounds for a fully hidden scheme and two tamed schemes, with tests to compare.
arxiv-2603-19144: Ding and co-authors tackle social bias inside large language models, not just in their outputs. Their method, UGID, treats the Transformer as a graph of attention routes and hidden states. It forces that graph to stay the same when only a sensitive trait changes in the input. Added limits on biased word scores help keep core meanings intact. Tests show less bias in and out of the training setting. The team reports that safety and general skill are kept.
arxiv-2603-19344: Bozyigit questions the fixed weighted sum at the heart of the classic artificial neuron. That sum acts like a mean, so noisy or extreme inputs can sway it. Two learnable swaps are offered: a power-weighted F-Mean rule and a distance-based Gaussian rule. Hybrid neurons blend the new rules with the linear sum through a learned dial. On CIFAR-10 and a noisy twin set, hybrids resist noise far better than the baseline. Scores reach 0.991 against 0.890 for standard neurons. Learned dials settle on sub-linear sums in most runs.
arxiv-2603-19844: Kumar and Aggarwal ask whether brain tumor models use the right MRI scans for each finding. Radiologists lean on contrast scans for enhancing tumor and FLAIR for swelling. Most networks fuse all scans in a fixed way, whatever the patient or region. The authors build a probing toolkit that ablates each scan by region. It also tracks gate paths inside the network. They find that adaptive hyper-connections push models toward the clinically apt scans. This pattern recurs across three backbones, and accuracy also improves.
arxiv-2603-20244: Vacaru argues that plain Einstein gravity can mimic many effects blamed on changed gravity laws. Changed theories are often read as proof that the standard Lambda CDM model falls short. Some f(R) models do fit the data better, he notes. His counter uses broader off diagonal solutions of the Einstein equations. A frame based method splits the hard equations so they can be integrated. The results carry extra constraints and effective constants. They can copy features of changed gravity and describe dark energy effects.
arxiv-2603-20444: Spiniello studies why ultra-compact massive galaxies show high stellar to dynamical mass ratios. Her sample holds 482 such galaxies from the INSPIRE surveys. She tests how the ratio shifts with compactness and velocity dispersion. Age, metal content, and star formation history also come in. First she uses a fixed virial factor to get dynamical masses. Then she lets that factor vary with radius and stellar mass. She also corrects stellar masses for shifts in the initial mass function.
arxiv-2603-20644: Chen and co-authors build ScaleEdit-12M, a large open dataset for instruction based image editing. Good edit data is hard to grow without costly closed tools. Their ScaleEditor system uses stacked agents that all run open source. Steps add world knowledge to source images and craft edit pairs. A task aware check then screens data quality. The set spans 23 task families across real and synthetic scenes. Fine tuning on it lifted scores on many edit benchmarks.
arxiv-2603-20844: Jaoua and co-authors build a Bayesian functional factor model for high dimensional longitudinal molecular data. Such data track many biomarkers over time in each patient. No past tool handled the time and dimension sides jointly. Their model pairs latent factors with functional principal components. Shared temporal programs run across variable subsets. Sparse priors keep factors readable and set their count by overspecification. An annealed variational method scales the inference. On COVID-19 hospital data it found clear patient groups in recovery paths.
arxiv-2603-21344: Braga-Neto proposes modeling an AI science community as a swarm of virtual labs. In this short note, each particle in the swarm is a full virtual lab. The labs explore as a group, much like real research communities do. The design uses swarm traits: no central control, a balance of search and use, and group behavior that emerges from local rules. He discusses how labs talk and sway each other, with citation-like voting, and ways to keep one lab from taking over.
arxiv-2603-21444: Bellavita and co-authors speed up sparse matrix multiplication, a core kernel in science and data work, on GPU supercomputers. In distributed runs, moving and merging partial products across nodes eats much of the time. Their Trident algorithm splits work with a hierarchy-aware scheme that leans on fast links inside a node. It also overlaps communication with computation. On the Perlmutter supercomputer, Trident ran up to 2.38 times faster than a standard 2D method and halved internode traffic.
arxiv-2603-22144: Ngambia and co-authors study how biochar pulls manganese from mine-affected water. Two routes can do the work: precipitation and surface binding. The team runs column and batch tests with oilseed rape straw biochars. Biochar made at 700 degrees removes about half the manganese. It raises the water's pH to 9, which triggers precipitation. Cooler biochars remove 20 to 30 percent at near-neutral pH. Atomistic simulations point to ion exchange and inner-sphere binding there. The results give design rules for targeted biochars.
arxiv-2603-22544: Goss and McKinnie compute how common visible lattice points are on flat slices of space. A lattice point counts as visible when the segment from the origin to it holds no other lattice point. The authors find an exact formula for the density on a single hyperplane, built from the Jordan totient function. They extend the result to crossings of several hyperplanes. They also treat points free of perfect powers, and map out which density values can occur at all.
arxiv-2603-22644: Zhu, Ohannessian, and Srebro study a PAC-Bayes learning rule for noisy binary classification. The rule balances training error against a distance between prior and posterior. At one balance setting it matches standard Bayesian prediction. The authors show that this Bayesian choice can overfit and keep excess loss from vanishing. A much stronger balance fixes that flaw. They map exactly how too little or too much regularization changes the outcome. The work extends earlier results from discrete priors to continuous ones.
arxiv-2603-23144: Zhao and co-authors model the steady radio sources tied to fast radio bursts in massive binaries. Some active burst sources seem to live in massive star pairs. Young magnetar wind nebulae can power the brighter steady sources, they find. Those magnetars would be a few decades old. Flux changes over time fit decay of the magnetar's inner field. Bow shocks explain the dimmer steady sources. Magnetic nebulae may emit X-rays detectable tens of megaparsecs away. Rotation-powered systems give much shorter detection ranges.
arxiv-2603-23244: Zhao and three co-authors study how people build reusable helpers while solving visual puzzles. In their online experiment, players defined helper constructions that capture repeating structure. Early on, players made many helpers and favored completeness over speed. With practice, helper use grew more selective and cheaper. Helpers let players crack puzzles that were otherwise too hard or impossible. Modeling backs the story: a program induction model with library learning tracks decision times and effort well. Raw program length predicts failure instead.
arxiv-2603-23644: Gilbert, Petigura, and Entrican hunt links between planet eccentricity and system layout in Kepler data. They focus on compact packs of small planets. Small planets on orbits under four days show signs of tidal rounding. That trend was firm for giant planets but is new for super-Earths. Two-planet systems run more eccentric than packs of three or more. Singles look more eccentric than multi-planet systems. No ties appear to period ratios, gap patterns, or size spread. The pattern hints at calm birth histories.
arxiv-2603-23744: Allard and Bölcskei characterize entropy and minimax risk for a broad class of compact pseudodifferential operators. Under decay and regularity conditions on the symbol, they link eigenvalue counts to phase-space volume. They then use a general link between spectra, entropy, and minimax risk. This gives explicit formulas for both quantities straight from the symbol. As an application, they extend Pinsker's theorem to unit balls in Sobolev spaces on unbounded domains, with constants set by phase-space geometry.
arxiv-2603-23844: Jiang and co-authors argue that language models should write programs, not raw planning files, for hard tasks. Models often turn problem text into PDDL for a solver, but scores drop as problems grow. The authors define unraveling problems, where a short text hides a huge PDDL file. Standard formalizers fail to scale on these. Their higher-order approach has the model write a small program that prints the large PDDL. This separates output length from problem size and improves results.
arxiv-2603-23944: Carey and co-authors boost a chip-scale magnetic sensor with a flux concentrator. Low-frequency magnetic fields matter for neuroscience, navigation, and Earth science, but they are weak. Their optomechanical magnetometer gains from the concentrator in two ways. It raises sensitivity and bandwidth. Its nonlinear response also shifts slow signals to higher frequencies, where the sensor works best and technical noise matters less. They report order-of-magnitude gains, with sensitivity below 20 nanotesla per root hertz down to 3 hertz.
arxiv-2603-24344: Terra and co-authors test whether initial-state geometry explains D-meson yields in small collision systems. In proton-proton and proton-lead collisions, D-meson yields grow faster than linearly with event activity. They model the events with a Monte Carlo generator based on kT-factorization. They try several spatial layouts of matter inside the proton and the lead nucleus. Every layout reproduces the data trend well, they find. They conclude this observable cannot pin down the spatial layout of matter in the proton.
arxiv-2603-24444: Yamagishi and co-authors introduce a model of discrete-time quantum walkers that interact with a localised magnetic impurity. Walkers affect each other only through the impurity, much as in the Kondo model. They first identify a quantum walker with a massless Dirac particle moving through delta potentials. A spin-half degree of freedom is then added at the origin. They derive all scattering matrices, solve bound states for a simple case, and simulate two-walker collisions. For XX-type coupling, entanglement between the walkers jumps sharply at collision.
arxiv-2603-24644: Patra and co-authors build a physics-informed neural network twin for distillation columns. The model predicts tray-by-tray behaviour of a binary column under transient conditions. Physics rules are built into the loss: vapour-liquid equilibrium by Raoult's law, tray mass and energy balances, and the McCabe-Thiele method. Training data is a synthetic set of 961 measurements over eight hours, from Aspen HYSYS with 16 sensor streams. An adaptive weighting scheme balances data fit and physics fit. Against five data-driven baselines, the twin achieves the lowest error.
arxiv-2603-24744: Bailey explores contrastive learning for weather data. Weather fields are high-dimensional and multimodal, so downstream tasks need compact shared forms. Contrastive learning can build robust embeddings from unlabelled data when labels are scarce. Prior work had not compared it with alternatives such as autoencoders, nor tested sparse data. Bailey studies contrastive learning on the ERA5 dataset in depth. The goal is embeddings that stay strong under sparsity and lift forecasting.
arxiv-2603-24844: Puri and co-authors train language models to reason over distributions of answers. Post-training often collapses a model's answer distribution onto one answer. That hurts tasks with several valid answers, such as medical diagnosis. Their multi-answer reinforcement learning changes the objective so the model emits several candidate answers in one pass, with confidence estimates. Inference-time search is internalised into generation. Across benchmarks, diversity, coverage, and calibration all improve over single-answer baselines.
arxiv-2603-24944: Gao and co-authors argue that flares can expand the habitable zone around low-mass stars. The classic zone tracks liquid water but ignores ultraviolet light, which prebiotic chemistry needs. Quiet low-mass stars emit too little ultraviolet across their water zones. Frequent flares can supply the missing flux. The authors refine the ultraviolet zone with a temperature-dependent model of RNA precursor synthesis, plus an empirical flare model. Applied to nine planets around Kepler flaring stars, three sit inside both zones without ozone depletion.
arxiv-2603-25044: Son and co-authors give robots a sense of heat with ThermoAct, a vision-language-action framework. Most robot models plan from sight and words alone, yet heat data can flag risk and reveal traits of objects. ThermoAct feeds thermal images into the plan. A large vision-language model reads the command, splits it into small steps, and steers the arm. This setup also makes data gathering for training more efficient. Real-world task trials show the approach works, with hints of better success and safety than sight-only systems.
arxiv-2603-25244: Liang and Pun armor images against transferable attacks with one fast sharpening pass. Attackers exploit flaws that many networks share, so a strike built on one model hits others. The pair finds that shared flaws point against the image's high-frequency Laplacian response. Boosting that response should cancel part of the flaw. Their Fast Preemptive Robustification does this with a single small convolution, no training or stand-in model. Untargeted attack success falls by about thirteen points. Targeted success drops from 10.7 to 4.1 percent.
arxiv-2603-25344: Stankevich, Studenikin, and Vyalkov build a field-theory account of how scattering blurs neutrino states in matter. Most treatments hold a neutrino's momentum fixed while it decoheres. Their generalized Lindblad equation lets momentum change as the particle scatters. Decoherence rates tie straight to scattering cross sections, which labs can bound. They run the frame on three cases: electrons, nucleons with exotic forces, and dark matter fermions. The blurring can reshape oscillation patterns a lot. It may also serve as a probe for new physics.
arxiv-2603-25644: Santilli studies limits of almost-critical sets in anisotropic isoperimetric problems. The setting uses convex norms that degenerate as they approach a general norm. The sets have fixed volume and finite perimeter. Their anisotropic mean curvature stays close to constant in an L-n sense. Santilli proves that any limit set is a finite union of disjoint Wulff shapes. The shapes may touch each other. The result is a rigidity statement for the accumulation points of such sequences.
arxiv-2603-25744: Zou and co-authors present MuRF, a way to use vision foundation models at several image scales at once. Most systems run inference at one fixed resolution. Low resolution favors broad scene meaning, while high resolution captures fine detail. MuRF runs a frozen model on multiple sizes of the same image. It then fuses the features into one representation. The method needs no training and fits many model families. The authors test it mainly on DINOv2 across many tasks. They also show it transfers to SigLIP2.
arxiv-2603-25844: Sharma and Mohanta study Majorana bound states where an altermagnet meets a superconductor. Their setting is a planar Josephson junction with a d-wave altermagnetic channel. In the topological regime, the near-zero states show a double-peak profile, with peaks near the interfaces. Simple models trace this shape to anisotropic hopping inside the altermagnet. The same trait appears in nanowire and T-shaped junctions. There, the states stay tied to interfaces rather than to junction shape. The authors see a route to Majorana networks with no external field.
arxiv-2603-25944: Vaddi tests whether small language models can reason about legal documents. Big models raise cost, latency, and privacy worries in legal work. He runs nine models under ten billion parameters on three legal benchmarks. Five prompting styles are tried across 405 experiments. A mixture-of-experts model using only 3B active parameters matches GPT-4o-mini on mean accuracy. It beats it on spotting legal holdings. The largest model, at 9B, does worst overall. Few-shot prompting helps most steadily, Vaddi reports. The whole study cost 62 dollars in API fees.
arxiv-2603-26844: Pace and co-authors test whether predicted uncertainty can flag bad frames in markerless biomechanics. Systems map 3D pose keypoints to anatomical landmarks, but usually report no confidence score. Using motion capture truth from AMASS, the team checked uncertainty at frame and joint level. Model uncertainty tracked landmark error closely, with a rank correlation near 0.63. Keeping only trusted frames cut error to about 16.8 mm. Severe failures were also detected with high accuracy.
arxiv-2603-26944: De Santis and co-authors add domain rules to predictive process monitoring through Logic Tensor Networks. Data-only models miss the sequential constraints that govern real event logs. Their method writes control-flow, temporal, and payload knowledge as logical formulas. A two-stage training scheme protects accuracy while the rules are learned. First, weighted axiom loss favors the data. Then rule pruning keeps only axioms that stay consistent and helpful. On four real event logs, the knowledge clearly improved predictions. Without the two stages, rules could badly hurt accuracy.
arxiv-2603-27044: Fraschini and co-authors compress RL policies by matching state occupancy instead of single actions. Deep RL policy spaces are huge and full of redundant settings. Earlier compression matched immediate actions, an error-prone proxy for behavior. Their occupancy-based method checks long-horizon state visitation mixtures directly. A uniqueness metric first curates a diverse pool of policies to learn from. The compression objective is smooth end to end. Tests on control benchmarks favor the occupancy approach.
arxiv-2603-27244: Dai and co-authors show that valley Chern numbers in valley photonic crystals are not quantized. Valley topology is defined locally near the K points, since global Chern numbers vanish. Half-integer valley Chern numbers had been widely assumed in the field. The team computed Berry curvatures across a continuous family of designs. The values form a continuous spectrum that shifts with structural parameters. Fine structures appear in the Berry curvature's momentum-space pattern. Cancellations within and between valleys explain this.
arxiv-2603-27844: Nitarach reports that prompt tricks fail next to raw model strength. Tests come from the AIMO 3 math contest setup. Three models face fifty IMO-level problems. Over twenty-three experiments try diverse prompt mixes. Every prompt-level fix falls short in the runs. High-temperature sampling already spreads errors enough. Weaker strategies cut accuracy more than correlation. An eight-point capability gap dominates all tuning. A verifier selector could recover selection loss.
arxiv-2603-28044: Kong and co-authors hunt for distant radio quasars by matching two large sky surveys. They cross-match radio sources from VLASS with deep optical images from Subaru's Hyper Suprime-Cam survey. Dropout color cuts yield about 400 candidates at redshift 4 and beyond, over some 1,200 square degrees. Most are too faint for SDSS. Extra matches at other radio bands show mostly flat spectra, and the counts thin out toward the earliest cosmic times.
arxiv-2603-28144: Calic, Coletti, and Sovilla report the first direct views inside a powder snow avalanche. High-speed cameras tracked single particles in the airborne layers of a natural slide. The flow splits into a brief surge, a churning suspension phase, and a wake. The team measures speeds, turbulence scales, and particle clustering across these phases. Large fluctuations trace to Kelvin-Helmholtz shear instability, and the shift to calm settling marks the layer's end. The data will sharpen avalanche models.
arxiv-2603-28344: Shang and Jiménez-Varón forecast high-dimensional functional time series in a way that stays readable. Such data, like age-specific death rates for many regions over years, mix time trends with cross links. Their method splits the series into a clear mean structure, split by factors like region and sex, plus a leftover process. A factor model forecasts the leftover part. On Japanese mortality data, the approach cut forecast error by 25 to 45 percent over a rival method.
arxiv-2603-28444: Di Gioia reframes retrieval for question answering as a hunt for the claim that cuts uncertainty most. Relevance ranking fails when sources conflict or the question itself is murky. His Entropic Claim Resolution scores each candidate claim by expected entropy drop across rival answers. The search stops once a set sufficiency line is crossed. Built into a production retrieval pipeline, the method offers a principled shift from most similar to most decisive evidence.
arxiv-2603-28544: Zhao and three co-authors build the full hierarchy of rational solutions for algebraic solitons in the massive Thirring model. Each level stacks N solitons of equal mass into one slow scattering pattern. The solutions come from double-Wronskian determinants, a new route for this model. The team proves each is set by a polynomial of degree N squared with 2N free parameters. Pole counts in each half-plane are fixed exactly, and the scattering unfolds on a square-root time scale.
arxiv-2603-28744: Barin-Pacela and co-authors argue that linear probes and sparse autoencoders fail at compositional generalization. Under superposition, concepts project from a wide space into fewer slots. A linear boundary in concept space need not stay linear after projection. Sparse autoencoders bake sparse inference into a fixed encoder, creating a steady gap. Tests show the main limit is dictionary learning, not inference. An oracle with a good dictionary solves the task at all scales tested. Tests used real activations from Pythia and Gemma models.
arxiv-2603-28844: Calculli and co-authors survey high school students in Apulia, Italy, on violence against women. Such violence is widespread and often goes unreported due to stigma and blame. The survey asks about gender roles, the acceptance of violence, and awareness in their communities. They study replies with a network method and an item response model. The two views show reply patterns and broad cultural trends. Traditional views remain common, most of all among young males. Parents' job status also links to stereotypes. The team calls for targeted action for youth.
arxiv-2603-29244: Mutisya and co-authors present the Thiomi Dataset for low-resource African languages. The corpus spans ten languages in four language families. It holds over 601,000 approved sentence annotations. It also includes more than 385,000 audio recordings. Over 100 contributors gathered data through a dedicated platform. The team trains speech recognition, translation, and speech synthesis baselines. Their best recognizer cut Swahili word error to 3.24 percent. That is down from a prior best of 8.3 percent.
arxiv-2603-29644: Yang and co-authors present Disentangled Graph Prompting for spotting out-of-distribution graphs. Models can fail badly when test data shift from training data. Graph detectors often train end-to-end with no odd examples to learn from. Their method instead prompts a pretrained graph encoder. Two prompt generators reshape edge weights of each input graph. One makes class-specific prompts, the other class-agnostic ones. Careful losses keep the prompts from trivial solutions. On ten datasets, their method beat the best baseline in AUC.
arxiv-2603-29844: Chen and co-authors present DIAL, a robot control frame that splits intent from action. Most vision-language-action models map inputs straight to motor commands. That wastes the model's high-level judgment and can erode its semantics. DIAL lets a slow system predict latent visual futures as an intent bottleneck. A light policy then turns intent plus current sight into actions. Two-stage training keeps optimization stable. On RoboCasa tasks, DIAL tops prior work with tenfold fewer demonstrations.
arxiv-2603-29944: Jin and co-authors sort quantum biomedical sensors into four generations. First devices use discrete energy levels but follow classical scaling. Second devices exploit coherence and reach the standard quantum limit. Third devices use entanglement and spin squeezing toward Heisenberg-limited precision. A fourth wave would fuse sensing with quantum learning and variational circuits. The authors match sensor bandwidths to neural signal layers. They also map bottlenecks and stage a milestone roadmap.
arxiv-2604-00044: Dvornikov works out how a warm neutrino gas with a nonzero chemical potential gives off Cherenkov plasmons. The host plasma is a slow gas of charged leptons, and field-theory amplitudes for the in and out states yield the energy loss rate. That rate covers longitudinal plasmons. For neutrino clusters that may form in the early universe via a light scalar boson, the process cools some clusters well, and Dvornikov maps the temperature range where this cooling channel holds.
arxiv-2604-00144: Nagarajan ranks the genitive forms of all 88 constellations recognized by the International Astronomical Union, by beauty, from an anonymous survey of 74 astronomers. Each new pair comparison is picked by active sampling to gain the most information, and scores update under Bayesian scoring. Pegasi wins overall, just ahead of Centauri and Andromedae, while Orionis, the early favorite, lands seventh. Gruis comes last, and the author adds notes on the sound and cultural weight of the top and bottom five, with hints of taste gaps by age group.
arxiv-2604-00344: Jiang and eleven colleagues propose Agent Q-Mix, a learning design turning layout selection into a joint learning problem. Each agent picks message actions forming a round message graph, using a layout-aware encoder, GRU memory, and Q-heads under central training with local running. Rewards balance scores against token cost. Across coding, logic, and math benchmarks, it tops rivals on scores with better token economy and failure strength, reaching about 21 percent on Humanity's Last Exam with Gemini-3.1-Flash-Lite, ahead of Microsoft Agent Framework and LangGraph at 19 percent.
arxiv-2604-00444: Kleinberg and colleagues analyse the social cost of algorithmic monoculture. Monoculture means many self-interested actors leaning on one common source of advice. In hiring-style matching markets, a more accurate shared signal can rationally attract everyone. Yet society as a whole would do better if each actor used less accurate but private advice. The authors generalise the Kleinberg-Raghavan model of one-sided matching with advice, and tackle its open question: quantifying the welfare loss from monoculture.
arxiv-2604-00744: Ford and colleagues introduce TacViT, a vision-transformer model for touch sensing on multi-fingered robot hands. Older approaches rely on convolutional networks that need large data sets for each new sensor and retraining when lenses, lighting, or wear change. TacViT uses global self-attention to read tactile images. It therefore judges contact properties on unseen sensors, cutting data collection and speeding up deployment.
arxiv-2604-01044: Alam, Bazilinska, and Bazilinskyy introduce CROWD, a curated dataset of minute, front-facing urban dashcam segments from public YouTube videos. It prioritizes routine driving and excludes crashes and other incident content. The release holds 51,753 records spanning 20,275.56 hours across 42,032 videos, covering 7,103 places in 238 countries and territories. They provide per-segment CSV files of machine detections for all 80 MS-COCO classes from YOLOv11x, plus local multi-object tracks. CROWD is shared as video identifiers with boundaries and annotations, enabling reproducible research without redistributing the videos.
arxiv-2604-01144: Rapakoulias, Liu, and Tsiotras revisit discrete-time Schrodinger bridges and density steering for Gaussian mixture boundary distributions. They build feasible Markovian policies that move an initial distribution to a final one as mixtures of component-to-component optimal policies, then optimize within that set. For minimum-effort steering their policy matches existing control costs, while for bridge problems it costs no more than prior methods and is less conservative.
arxiv-2604-01344: Watkiss-Leek and colleagues build IDEA2, a workflow for drawing competency questions out of domain experts without exhausting them. A language model first drafts questions from requirement documents, experts review and reshape them on a shared platform, and rejected questions are rewritten until agreement emerges. Every edit, anonymous comment and generation setting is logged for provenance. Trials in scientific data and cultural heritage show faster requirements work, with questions experts accept more readily.
arxiv-2604-01644: Liao and colleagues define text-to-OSM location, finding exact 2D spots in urban places from textual scene notes alone. They present TOL, a large-scale benchmark spanning many regions, with about 121K textual queries paired with OSM map tiles over about 316 km of road routes across three cities. They propose TOLoc, a coarse-to-fine location method using the meanings of nearby objects and their compass information. Tests show TOLoc beats the best method by 6.53 percent at the 5 m threshold, with gains at 10 m and 25 m.
arxiv-2604-01844: Pieta and colleagues present FaCT-GS, a fast CT system using Gaussian Splatting, a rendering technique adapted to X-ray CT. Splatting benefits rarely justify switching from older algorithms. FaCT-GS optimizes voxelization and rasterization pipelines, running faster than earlier methods and scaling well with projection and volume size. Improved voxelization fits Gaussians rapidly to existing volumes, as a warm-start prior or compressed form. The method runs over 4 times faster than splatting CT on standard projections, and over 13 times faster on 2k projections.
arxiv-2604-01944: Zubow, Angjo, Dimce and Dressler rebuild wideband wireless channel responses from patchy snapshots. When interference blanks subbands, their physics informed Transformer fills the gaps, treating subband interference as a bursty two state Markov chain and attending along both axes. A composite loss ties spectral accuracy, delay profile shape, impulse sparsity and smooth time behavior, while varied speeds teach mobility. Against carry forward, zero fill and spline baselines it reached the best match, at interference up to 50 percent, beating the best rival and degrading gently across speeds.
arxiv-2604-02044: Neamtu, Kuehn, Landi and Rudik study Kuramoto oscillators driven by rough noise. They prove that phases and frequencies converge to sync at an exponential rate, give that rate in explicit form, and size the random basin of attraction. Long term behavior, they show, follows the mean of the phases. A Lyapunov function that depends only on noise intensity, not its fine structure, drives the proof, and simulations illustrate the results and possible extensions.
arxiv-2604-02244: Baumgartner and Verwer learn state machines from data streams, where data arrive over time rather than all at once. Their generic method pairs a merge heuristic using sketches for incomplete prefix trees with an open source state merging library. Tests on a known open dataset show gains in run time, memory use and result quality over existing methods. A formal analysis proves the method learns within the PAC framework and improves run time without sacrificing correctness at larger sample sizes.
arxiv-2604-02344: Maczan characterizes WebGPU dispatch overhead for language model inference at batch size one. WebGPU per operation validation compounds across the many small dispatches in neural inference, yet naive benchmarks overstate dispatch cost. A sequential dispatch method reveals the true cost, with backend choice dominating and implementation choice mattering within backends. On Vulkan, kernel fusion lifts throughput by 53 percent while CUDA fusion gives no gain, confirming per operation overhead as a key differentiator. A new PyTorch backend and compiler reach about a tenth of CUDA performance.
arxiv-2604-02644: Al-Jarrah and four colleagues offer conditional Wasserstein autoencoders, a tool for simulation under set conditions that exploits low-dimensional structure. The tool works on both the output variables and the variables they depend on. A block-triangular decoder plus an independence rule for latent variables lets the decoder itself draw samples for chosen conditions. Tests show large error cuts over the low-rank ensemble Kalman filter, above all when the measures at hand are truly low-dimensional. The work suits cases where data live near a low-dimensional shape.
arxiv-2604-03244: Jiang and colleagues argue that AI testing needs item-level data as standard practice, not just overall scores. Without item text, test setup, answers, and score stats, validity claims cannot be checked, and inflated claims about skill go uncaught. They build OpenEval, a store of more than 10 million answers across 160,000 items, and show item data can expose weak items and skewed constructs.
arxiv-2604-03544: Yen develops a method for sizing up left-out factor bias in curved IV tools. It covers the local mean treatment effect, the treated version, and the partly linear IV model. He works out bias breakdowns, partial ID bounds, and OVB-adjusted trust intervals, figured with double machine learning. Applied to the US JTPA trial, first-stage follow-through proves robust to left-out factors. Treatment effects prove more shaky, with female impacts robust and male impacts fragile.
arxiv-2604-03644: Guo and colleagues argue that a magnet's pull can induce a Hall response by shaping crashes between neutral non-chiral quasiparticles, as seen in gases. In layered honeycomb WS2 and perovskite LiNbO3, thermal flow parts peak at nearly the same temperature. Transverse thermal drag in clean, simple crystals matches basic constants over binding energy pack. In complex, dirty crystals it runs much larger and varies strongly with temperature. Peak thermal Hall angle stays roughly the same in all crystals.
arxiv-2604-03744: Luiz Carlos Ryff argued that events set apart in time, rather than in space, can shed light on a long-standing puzzle about linked particles. The puzzle concerns pairs of particles whose measured traits match in ways that seem to defy distance, as in the Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen setup. Despite many papers on the topic, rival readings of those linked results still coexist without agreement. Ryff worked through the standard rules of the theory step by step and showed how time-separated events help make sense of the strange links.
arxiv-2604-03844: Jinwook Kim mechanized cross-domain state preservation in Isabelle/HOL as a functor. The goal is simple: a freeze, seizure, or confiscation on a tokenized asset must hit every domain holding it or none at all. State machines serve as objects and synchronization maps as morphisms, with identity, composition, and associativity as theorems. Safety, liveness under bounded Byzantine faults, convergence from arbitrary states, and a hierarchy of functors follow. Ten theory files build cleanly, with the refinement to code still unproven.
arxiv-2604-04044: Tianhao Liang and team surveyed the low-altitude economy, where cellular-connected drones serve watching, freight, and rescue work. Dead zones, random signal clash, and scarce spectrum threaten links that steady flight depends on. Their comms-control co-design plan uses a three-layer design: advance planning before flight, live action in flight, and system-level steering of resources. Early case studies showed the co-design raised toughness of drone systems a lot.
arxiv-2604-04244: Egor Fokin and Manolis Savva built VisACD, a visibility-based, rotation-equivariant, intersection-free algorithm for approximate convex decomposition with GPU acceleration. Collision detection trades accuracy against speed, and primitive colliders like bounding boxes are fast while raw meshes are costly. Prior methods give high-quality results but need many convex parts and react to mesh orientation. VisACD yields high-quality splits with fewer parts, ignores shape facing, and runs more efficiently than prior work.
arxiv-2604-04544: Lubat and colleagues propose a modular approach for supply chain work based on Product Time Petri Nets. Each part is modeled alone, with global flow rising through synchronized transition labels. A key feature models the supply chain manager as a critical shared and mobile resource whose presence directly affects system feasibility. The team studies how timing constraints and manager capacity shape flow, spotting configurations leading to success, timeouts, or timelocks. The approach enables what-if analysis of coordination policies, showing Product Time Petri Nets suit synced timed systems.
arxiv-2604-04744: Shang and Chen model randomness beacons built on verifiable delay functions as a cost problem, not just a crypto problem. A foe who buys faster hardware may still profit, even when the delay code is sound. They cast the attack choice as a best-stop problem, prove best play follows a cutoff rule, and derive tight tests linking delay length to foe costs and prize odds. Grinding, selective abort, and rival foes each raise the prize, so safe delays must grow; the pair close with rules for picking them.
arxiv-2604-04944: Madani and three colleagues address unstable preferences in language models answering multiple-choice questions. Plausible distractors pull attention toward wrong options, making models flip between right and wrong answers. Their Inclusion-of-Thoughts method filters choices step by step, rebuilding each question from plausible options alone. That controlled setting lets researchers compare judgments and test how stable the model's inner reasoning stays under perturbation. By documenting the filtering openly, the method aims to steady model preferences and focus attention on credible answers.
arxiv-2604-05044: Ayala and Pineda find the size of the leading infrared renormalon of the chromomagnetic moment of a heavy quark. They give values of higher order terms of the series. They compute the hyperfine splitting of the B and D mesons for the ground state with hyperasymptotic precision, including the leading term tied to the first renormalon. Fitting lab data to the operator product expansion, with one free parameter, they obtain a value of 0.507 square GeV for the ground state.
arxiv-2604-05544: Ma and seven colleagues make robot visuomotor policies recover from execution errors by accepting sparse human or planner pointing cues mid-task. Their ReV framework pairs a global diffusion head that plants action anchors with a local head that interpolates between them, replanning at every step. Trained only by perturbing expert demos, it raises success rates on hard simulated and real tasks.
arxiv-2604-05644: Cohen, Müller, and Papini study long-run behavior of random wave, Schrödinger, and Maxwell equations on the sphere. Testing time-steppers against trace formulas for energy, mass, and momentum, they prove Euler-Maruyama schemes fail the long-run test. The random exponential integrator keeps correct long-run behavior, backed by number tests.
arxiv-2604-05844: Pandey and Chandola model patient care paths with Transformer Hawkes processes in continuous time. Transformer history coding plus Hawkes dynamics jointly predict event type and timing, while inverse square-root class weights lift rare-event sensitivity without resampling data. Real-world tests show better performance and clearer high-risk patient signals.
arxiv-2604-05944: Sengupta and Pautov prove a case of a 1997 guess by Goreinov, Tyrtyshnikov, and Zamarashkin on square submatrices of tall matrices with orthonormal columns. They show a two-column case always holds for any height, with a chosen square piece whose smallest singular value stays at least one over the square root of the height. All middle cases stay open except the tiny four-by-two case, already known.
arxiv-2604-06044: Bašić and Ilić study the general reduced second Zagreb index of trees. It is a sum over edges built from vertex degrees plus a parameter. Their 2026 paper extends and corrects earlier equality results on the smallest value of this index. The trees have a given vertex count and maximum degree, with the parameter at least negative one. They add two distinct approaches for molecular trees of maximum degree three and four at parameter negative two. They also characterize the trees attaining the minimum.
arxiv-2604-06244: Cruz and twelve colleagues present Apptainer training for physics staff. Built for analysis preservation, the tasks run common high-energy and nuclear physics tools inside containers, bringing reproducibility, portability, collaboration, and resource efficiency. The module, Introduction to Apptainer/Singularity, sits in the HEP Software Foundation Training Center, which gives new high-energy physics staff software skills and good habits.
arxiv-2604-06444: Villar, Singh, Ozdemir, Sichitiu, and Güvenç field-test LoRaWAN, a long-range wireless network, at AERPAW, Lake Wheeler Field and Centennial Campus. A vehicle, a 50-meter drone, and a helikite at 150 and 300 meters show how height, motion, and terrain affect reception. They track signal strength and SNR against distance and spreading factor, fitting a log-distance model to vehicle data from rural and urban NLOS settings. The steady helikite gives the most reliable links, while drone and vehicle links vary more with motion and multipath.
arxiv-2604-06544: Paleari da Silva studies Vekua-type operators built from diagonal operators on compact Lie groups. He gives criteria for when such cases with fixed coefficients are globally hypoelliptic, which means their solutions stay smooth, and globally solvable, which means their equations have solutions. He also gives enough conditions for solvability when coefficients change. In short, the paper maps when solutions stay smooth and when they can be found at all in this family.
arxiv-2604-06644: Guo and five colleagues protect shared-model inputs from being reused for other tasks. Their framework squeezes inputs through a variational bottleneck trained without rebuilding pixels, keeping accuracy for one chosen classifier. A dynamic binary mask, built from KL divergence and saliency scores, blocks latent traits that do not serve that classifier. On CIFAR-100, chosen-classifier utility stays strong while all unintended classifiers fall below 2 percent, a suppression ratio above 45 times.
arxiv-2604-06744: Mamun and Hansen improve speech enhancement for cochlear implant recipients with DAT-CFTNet. Human hearing picks out key speech while sidelining noise, and their dual-path attention module in the network's bottleneck mimics that focus. DAT-RNN attention, joined to a modified complex-valued frequency transformation network, separates speech from noise across time-frequency regions using local and global context. Tests show steadier gains in intelligibility and quality over CFTNet and DCCRN, including for implant listeners with severely limited hearing restoration, while cutting non-stationary noise without musical artifacts.
arxiv-2604-07344: Jelson and seven colleagues release NIRVANA, a dataset that reconstructs how students actually use generative AI while writing essays. It follows 77 students through an analytical essay task with ChatGPT, recording keystrokes, full chat histories, and every passage copied from the model. Analysis finds varied query habits linked to essay length and readability, and sorts writers into four profiles: Lead Authors, Collaborators, Drafters, and Vibe Writers. A replay tool lets researchers step through each writing process in full.
arxiv-2604-07444: Kervyn and Stieberger analyze fixed-angle high-energy form of n-point tree-level string amplitudes. They use saddle-point analysis and step rules in motion inputs. Small numbers in long-run series in inverse string tension follow Bernoulli-number data, not multiple zeta values of the low-energy regime. Resurgence theory lifts wild series to transseries whose Stokes data capture a link between unreal and real regions. They derive them for four-point open string cases. A double-copy form for closed-string amplitudes follows via Lefschetz thimbles.
arxiv-2604-07644: Fang and Chou present GPU-SLS, a GPU tool for safe predictive control for unsure robots and long spans. The method tunes a path, a tracking control, and an in-reach set under noise, all in real time. A quadratic planning method with a GPU fast solver uses side-by-side linked scans and caching. Times fall 97.7 percent versus CPU solvers and 71.8 percent versus GPU solvers, while SLS-based control and reach speed up 237-fold, with 100 percent safety on four-legged robots and human-like robots.
arxiv-2604-07744: Li and Cao develop a geometric framework linking objective accuracy to structure recovery in prototype-based clustering. The analysis works for many loss functions and no single algorithm. Their condition number compares cluster scale against the smallest loss rise needed to push a point across a boundary. When that number is small, a near-best solution must also sort points nearly as well as a benchmark split. The work also exposes a tradeoff between toughness and sensitivity to cluster imbalance, with sharp jumps for exact recovery.
arxiv-2604-07844: Cruts and three colleagues model how plug structure and blood flow jointly govern fibrin buildup during clotting. A growing aggregate is patchy, with dense and loose zones, and active platelet surfaces host the reactions that build the fibrin network holding the clot firm. Their 2D framework joins a discrete pre-adhered mass, a reduced clotting model that makes thrombin, and a fibrin buildup model. Three plug setups with set gaps between platelets are tested across wall shear rates. Results measure when and where clotting takes hold in space and time.
arxiv-2604-07944: Afsharrad and three colleagues distill motion-planning skill from a large teacher model into a smaller student for autonomous vehicles. Large models show promise by treating trajectory prediction as language generation, but onboard systems cannot run them. Building on GPT-Driver, which turns scenes into language prompts and generates waypoint paths with chain-of-thought reasoning, the team compares two student training paradigms. On-policy generalized knowledge distillation trains the student on its own outputs with dense teacher feedback. A dense-feedback reinforcement approach offers a second route.
arxiv-2604-08444: Nha, Hue, Phuong, and Hong study lepton flavor violating decays in an extended 3-4-1 model with a new charged Higgs boson and minimal inverse seesaw neutrinos. The model fits current limits on magnetic moments for electrons and muons. It also fits flavor violating decays of charged leptons, the Higgs boson, and the Z boson. Its predictions tie those observables together for future tests, with the tau to muon gamma bound already pinning the muon deviation near one part in a billion.
arxiv-2604-09244: Zheng and colleagues ask whether 2D or 3D inputs govern salience in vision-language-action models. Recent models expanded from 2D-only to 2D plus 3D inputs, improving spatial perception but sharply increasing token counts. Existing pruning schemes target 2D-only models and ignore differences in 2D/3D salience. The authors develop a tri-stage analysis of salience, then a tri-stage pruning framework for optimal token selection. Experiments show up to two and a half times faster inference with minimal accuracy loss and about 6 percent overhead.
arxiv-2604-09344: Nakata and colleagues propose DialogueSidon, a model for getting back full-duplex talk tracks from degraded monaural two-speaker audio. Clean split tracks are a key resource for speech research but hard to collect at scale. Most in-the-wild talk survives only as damaged mixes. DialogueSidon jointly fixes and splits such audio. It combines a variational autoencoder on self-supervised speech features with a spread model that rebuilds speaker-wise versions from the mixture. Tests show better clarity and splitting quality over a baseline, with faster use.
arxiv-2604-09444: Eleftheriou, Pallis, and Constantinides study confidence without competence in AI work. Large language models are widely used by students, yet fast answers may discourage reflection. The authors examine how alternative designs support deeper thinking without raising burden. In phase one, interviews with 16 students informed Deep3, with modes: future-self explanations, contrastive learning, and guided hints. In phase two, 85 participants found a standard baseline produced high felt grasp despite the lowest learning. Future-self notes best aligned felt and actual grasp, while guided hints gave the largest gains.
arxiv-2604-09744: Qian, Fang, and Li present MPAC, a set of rules for agents that serve many owners. Current rules assume one owner, so free agents fall back to ad hoc chat or silent loss. MPAC sets rules across five layers. It makes stating intent needed before action and supports human-in-the-loop review. It defines 21 message types, three state trackers, Lamport-clock causal stamps, and shared-access control. A three-agent code-review benchmark shows 95 percent lower teamwork costs and 4.8 times wall-clock speedup over a human-run bar.
arxiv-2604-10044: Xu and nine co-authors study long-context reading falling into stuck loops. Fallen focus drives the failure: heads lock onto a narrow history suffix, held by cache reuse. Since cache policies rank by focus weight, collapse pumps repeat tokens' scores, feeding loops. LoopBench gauges loop depth and output wobble beyond downstream scores. LoopGuard, a lightweight plug-in cache guard, detects loop onset and breaks the cycle by pruning repeat tail spans. It cuts loop rate by over 90 points while bringing back variety and cutting token waste.
arxiv-2604-10344: Bilalpur and six colleagues compare old and deep ways of vision depression detection across contexts. The old way uses handmade cues such as facial looks with support vector models, while the deep way uses learnt cues from vision models. They test both on mother-child talks in the TPOT data and doctor talks in the Pitt data. The old way scores higher in both contexts and is fairer in the doctor context. Cross-context reach stays modest for both, hinting it may depend on context.
arxiv-2604-11044: Fu and six colleagues present SVA Generator, translating SystemVerilog descriptions into executable SVAs. Verification dominates chip work cost. SVAs matter for watching runs and checking, yet hand-writing them is slow and error-prone. Prompting language models is unreliable, yielding SVAs that are syntactically invalid or semantically wrong, worsened by domain data. SVA Generator uses AST-grounded constraint injection and a check pipeline. Checks keep order and cut errors through constraint checks. A benchmark suite grouped by AST depth, judged by match checking, splits semantic truth from syntax form.
arxiv-2604-11144: Zhong and three colleagues propose knowledge-enhanced clustering, a method that builds concept knowledge with language models. Traditional methods focus on visual knowledge and coarse labels, making it hard to distinguish similar-looking but different classes. The method first condenses labels into abstract concepts. It then extracts discriminative attributes for each concept and similar pairs via prompts. Applied to each input image, the knowledge gives features that combine with visual features for clustering. Evaluated on 20 datasets, it improves existing methods. Without training, it beats CLIP on 14 of 20 datasets.
arxiv-2604-11344: Chen and four colleagues protect embedding-as-a-service offerings with GeoMark, a watermarking framework that uses geometry to place marks locally. Older marks fail three ways: trigger marks break under paraphrasing, transform marks shift with dimension changes, and region marks can fire by chance. GeoMark sets an in-manifold embedding as the mark target, builds anchors set apart by clear margins, and injects the mark inside local neighborhoods. Tests on four benchmarks preserve utility and geometric fidelity while keeping verification robust under paraphrasing, shifts, and clustering-selection-elimination attacks.
arxiv-2604-11444: Liu and four colleagues present HuiYanEarth-SAR, the first foundation model generating SAR imagery worldwide from coordinates alone. It injects geo priors to control large-scale structure. It models scattering in the background to keep fine textures authentic. The goal is high fidelity in global meaning and fine scattering. No other inputs are needed. The work builds an efficient SAR simulator bridging geography, scattering physics, and AI. It shifts SAR research from perception toward simulation and creation, toward a trusted digital twin of Earth.
arxiv-2604-11844: Ahmed, Al-Badawi, and Sakallı map geodesic motion and epicyclic oscillations around an Einstein-Skyrme black hole in anti-de Sitter spacetime. Horizon structure falls into three regimes, with transitions governed by the charge-like parameter rather than the Skyrme coupling. The radial epicyclic frequency grows at large radius and overtakes the orbital frequency, flipping the sign of periastron precession, a signature absent in flat asymptotics. Fitting twin-peak oscillation data from four sources gives a charge-like value near 0.6 and orbital radii near 4.2 mass units.
arxiv-2604-11944: Pryor, Breton, and El Fathi present DIAX, a standard JSON-based format for unifying diabetes time-series data across devices. Continuous glucose monitors, smart insulin pens, and automated insulin delivery systems all produce rich time-series data, but inconsistent formats block sharing and analysis. DIAX covers glucose, insulin, and meal signals, promotes interoperability and reuse, and ships open-source tools for conversion, compatibility, and visualisation. It already supports major datasets totalling over 10 million patient-hours, while remaining a translational resource rather than a data host.
arxiv-2604-12044: Corn and Weinshall address Trajectory Deviation, where training drops general states for data groups, losing learned features without classic overfit signals. Their VISTA setup keeps training on track using a check-guided Marginal Coverage score to find expert anchors, earlier states keeping skill over distinct data regions. A reach-weighted anchor set joins online, smoothing the loss landscape and saving learned knowledge. Across benchmarks, VISTA lifts toughness and general results over standard training and prior self-teaching, cutting storage cost by 90 percent without quality loss.
arxiv-2604-12444: Moonseok Choi and Yoshiyuki Y. Yamaguchi infer hidden traits of linked oscillators from response data. Their set-up is a large group of Stuart-Landau oscillators, simple models of rhythm units. They watch the linear response of one unit and of a group-wide measure. Link strength follows from the single-unit response. The spread of natural rates follows from the group-wide response. Only one-dimensional readings are needed in the two-dimensional set-up. Computer tests back the inference theory.
arxiv-2604-12544: Adel Ali and Alexey Belyanin propose pairing electrons via magnetic flux fluctuations. Flat electron sheets sit beside an LC resonator's inductor. Vacuum fluctuations of its quantized flux create long-range attraction. Attraction acts between angular momentum states. Pairing follows in a broad class of materials. Pairing survives to a few Kelvin or higher, depending on field area. The state is a pair-density wave topological chiral superconductor. The circuit QED platform offers a tool for new quantum phases.
arxiv-2604-12744: Terra Blevins and 13 colleagues build Universal NER v2, a multilingual named entity benchmark. Gold-standard test data remain scarce in most languages. The Universal NER project, now in its fourth year, collects standard cross-lingual annotations. A general tagset and thorough guidelines govern named entity spans. UNER v1, the first installment, appeared in 2024. The project has since grown into an active community.
arxiv-2604-12944: Yiyang Huang and six colleagues survey hallucinations in video language models. Hallucinations look plausible yet contradict the input video. Two core types organize the field: dynamic distortion and content fabrication, each with two subtypes. The survey reviews benchmarks, metrics, and fixes for evaluation and mitigation. Weak time representation and thin visual grounding drive both types. Motion-aware encoders and counterfactual learning point the way forward.
arxiv-2604-13044: Djerrab, Gritti, and Benzenati test Chia's green branding by measuring the blockchain's real energy and carbon footprint. Combining testbed experiments with models of running and embodied emissions, they find yearly carbon output 18 times the claimed figure, at 0.88 million tonnes, far above other blockchains marketed as green. The initialization phase and ongoing operations, not just mining-style work, drive the excess.
arxiv-2604-13144: Hasselgren and Koczor adapt randomized quantum time-evolution algorithms to classical tensor-network simulation, aiming for massive parallelization. Their MPS TE-PAI approach evolves time exactly on average through ensembles of randomized shallow Trotter-variant circuits, with sampling of circuit variants as the only randomness and no shot noise. On disordered one-dimensional spin rings, per-sample gate counts fall by up to a factor of 1,000 against Trotterized MPS evolution. The method resists severe bond-dimension truncation better than product formulas.
arxiv-2604-13244: Kiefer and colleagues summarize the fourth Maritime Computer Vision workshop, held as part of CVPR 2026, with five benchmark challenges stressing forecast accuracy and on-device real-time feasibility. The report covers challenge setup, scoring protocols, datasets, and benchmark tracks, with numeric results, qualitative contrasts, and cross-challenge analyses of new method trends. Technical reports from top teams highlight practical design choices and lessons learned across the benchmark suite.
arxiv-2604-13444: Salehi, Ciabattoni, and Monticone show how nonlocal photonic time crystals can open momentum bandgaps of infinite extent with minimal modulation speed and strength. Momentum bandgaps, the twin of frequency gaps in spatial crystals, were hard to observe because they demanded fast, strong tuning. The authors trace that demand to Manley-Rowe relations, then show tuning the plasma frequency of a Lorentz material removes it. Adding spatial spread removes all remaining constraints.
arxiv-2604-13644: McIntyre, Sarkar, and Loss review spin qubits and the road to scaling them. Spin qubits appeal through long coherence times, small footprints, and compatibility with semiconductor manufacturing. The review covers single electron-spin, hole-spin, donor, and multispin encodings, and how confinement and strain in heterostructures create addressable spin levels. It weighs long-range coupling routes, including circuit QED hybrids, Andreev qubits, and spin shuttling, and closes with linking qubits via topological spin textures.
arxiv-2604-13944: Feng offers a book-length treatment of high-dimensional data under elliptical symmetry, a family that covers heavy tails and gaps from Gaussian models. Robust tools built on spatial signs, spatial ranks, and Kendall's tau matrices anchor the methods, from location and covariance estimation to sphericity tests, factor pricing, change points, and dimension reduction. Older low-dimensional and high-dimensional benchmarks are surveyed before the robust options are built. The book aims at graduate students and other readers who need inference beyond the Gaussian picture.
arxiv-2604-14144: Li and eighteen colleagues present SpatialEvo, a self-evolving framework for three-dimensional spatial reasoning built around a deterministic geometric environment. Because scene geometry fixes ground truth exactly from point clouds and camera poses, the environment turns raw scenes into noise-free oracles instead of trusting model consensus. A shared policy plays both questioner and solver under geometric checks, while a scheduler drills the weakest task types. Tests across nine benchmarks top the averages at both 3B and 7B scales.
arxiv-2604-14244: Feng and Tang study second-order iterative functional equations, seeking smooth solutions whose derivatives stay bounded. Using the fiber contraction result and Faà di Bruno's formula, they establish bounded C-n solutions with bounded derivatives from order one to n. The paper treats equations built from iterates of the unknown function plus a nonlinear term.
arxiv-2604-14444: Wulnye and five colleagues stress-test four intrusion detectors for IoT networks under data poisoning on three real-world IoT data sets. Ensemble methods hold fairly steady, but logistic regression and deep neural networks lose up to 40 percent under label tampering and outlier attacks. Poisoning warps decision boundaries, blurs detection, and weakens deployment readiness. The authors call for attack-hardened training, steady anomaly watch, and feature-level checks, plus resilience testing inside regulatory codes for AI-driven IoT security.
arxiv-2604-14644: Bae, Lee, and Yang propose CURaTE, a method for continual real-time unlearning that preserves language-model knowledge. Existing methods ignore continuous, immediate action, so utility degrades as updates pile up and sensitive information stays exposed. CURaTE trains a sentence embedding model to draw sharp decision boundaries for spotting prompts matching forget requests. Prompt similarity to forget requests decides between answering and refusing. By never modifying model parameters, CURaTE forgets better than existing methods, keeps knowledge nearly perfect over any number of updates, and alone manages continual real-time unlearning.
arxiv-2604-14744: Li and five colleagues propose an inverse-design route to scattering exceptional points in a two-port resonant system holding a single mode. Such points in non-Hermitian photonics, where wave amplitude and phase control turns unconventional, are usually hard to hunt down across a multidimensional parameter space. Their method tunes geometric parameters directly to land on the points. Full-wave simulation and an equivalent circuit model both confirmed the approach. In principle it extends to multi-mode systems and a broad class of resonant devices.
arxiv-2604-14944: Lim and eight others present HRDexDB, a 4D dexterous grasping dataset for human and robot hands. It captures hand-object trajectories across five embodiments, with 3,200 trials over 100 objects. A multi-camera system and pipeline supply multi-view and egocentric RGB views, hand geometry, robot states, object poses, and outcome annotations. Human and robot hands share objects, enabling study of grasp strategies and contact patterns across embodiments. Demos cover human-to-robot contact-map transfer, robot-object contact estimation, and retrieval-assisted grasping, making HRDexDB a dexterous-interaction resource.
arxiv-2604-15044: McDonald and Gonzalez introduce CoGrid and the Multi-User Gymnasium for multi-agent experimentation. Human-AI interaction studies need accessible tooling, but researchers lack tools for experiments where humans and AI act together. CoGrid is a multi-agent grid-based simulation library with dual NumPy and JAX backends. The Multi-User Gymnasium turns such simulations into interactive web experiments with any number of humans and AI, using server-authoritative or peer-to-peer networking with rollback netcode for latency. Both tools are open source, with case studies showing their utility.
arxiv-2604-15344: Vishwarupe and three colleagues interview 33 designers and developers at three large tech firms about how they decide to use large language models. People judged not just capability but the role a model would play. As a tool under clear human control, use felt acceptable. As a teammate with fuzzy agency, it raised worries about who answers for outcomes. The study frames this as a design-time positioning problem, with a rubric for authority and oversight.
arxiv-2604-15744: Sidney Wong's thesis studies how language tracks place identity in New Zealand-related Reddit communities. Blending user interviews with computational methods, it examines lexical, grammatical, and meaning-based variables in how members speak. Users broadly link language to place, and place-based groups form one continuous speech community, though the match with geographic dialects stays complex. The work also built a corpus of 4.26 billion raw words and shows social media can serve as a live lab for studying language change.
arxiv-2604-15844: Kosz, Niksiński, and Wróbel prove uniform upper and lower bounds for Delannoy numbers. These count lattice points in high-dimensional cross-polytopes, also called hyper-octahedrons or l1 balls. Their dimension-free count then yields dimension-free estimates for discrete maximal functions over cross-polytopes. A comparison with the continuous setting extends the estimate to all lp spaces for large radii. They also treat the full maximal function for small radii and the dyadic version for any radii.
arxiv-2604-15944: Ahn and four colleagues present CIMple, a fully digital SRAM-based compute-in-memory accelerator for self-attention in transformers. Edge devices struggle to run large language models, and existing compute-in-memory designs handle only static multiply-accumulate operations. CIMple adds a dual-banked design with 8-bit parallel weight feeding and a look-up-table implementation of the split softmax for attention. A 32kb accelerator built in 28nm reaches 26.1 TOPS/W with INT8 precision, cutting latency with minimal accuracy loss.
arxiv-2604-16144: C. A. S. Almeida offers a slow-speed frame where collapse comes from a set instability caused by gravity pulling on itself, curbed by short-range pushback. A nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a pushback part governs high-density dynamics. With a Gaussian ansatz, he derives an energy formula; spread states lose stability past a key mass. This loss marks a width split, yielding localized states. Collapse then means picking one attractor, driven by tiny asymmetries without noise or coupling. The mechanism extends Schrödinger-Newton models, dodging bad behavior.
arxiv-2604-16244: Zhang and Hu present the latest results from FASER, an LHC project, from Run 3 data. They report leading limits in a dark-photon search. They also measure how often neutrinos interact, and run a first search for charm hadrons made when neutrinos hit a tungsten emulsion setup. In addition, they report the first electron neutrino seen in the electronic part, and the first detailed look at muon neutrino interactions by energy and rapidity.
arxiv-2604-16744: Woo and colleagues present a framework testing tuned personalization of readings with fake learners. The system builds an ontology of goals and parts from open textbooks in an Ontology Atlas. It labels textbook chunks with ontology tags and makes reading-assessment pairs. Simulated readers learn through a memory model with reader factors, error fixes and ease, while know-how tracking drives adaptation. Answers come from score-based selection over the learner's memory state. Adaptive reading lifted computing, gained murkily in chem, and stayed flat or down in biology.
arxiv-2604-16844: Sundermann and colleagues show UCd11 is a strongly localized uranium 5f3 system, an antiferromagnetic intermetallic. Its uranium-uranium spacings run nearly twice the Hill limit, hinting weakly hybridized 5f nature and uranium adopts the formal U3+ configuration. Density working theory plus moving mean-field theory math, tuned to valence-band photo spectra, prove the localization. Core-level spectra from an Anderson flaw model show satellite structures are not a safe sign of strong correlations or roaming 5f ways.
arxiv-2604-17044: Haydys, He, and Salm prove a rigidity result for critical Z/2 eigensections of the Laplacian on a sphere, tied to a flat real line bundle over a branch-point configuration. Every minimal non-degenerate one is deformation rigid: any small deformation of the configuration that still admits one must come from an SO(3) rotation. The result extends this phenomenon found earlier in symmetric examples of Taubes and Wu.
arxiv-2604-17144: Li, Zhang, and Tuo develop a frequentist scheme for validating computer models overall and in parts. Their FMMT estimates the gap between model and physical process with kernel ridge regression, then tests weighted Fourier coefficients by frequency. Theory gives normal limits for the coefficients, hence direct p-values, and tests on simulations and a shear-layer test show high power, tight error control, and keen local response.
arxiv-2604-17244: Gurjar, Ishmam, and Marino present DORA Explorer, a training-free method boosting agent search.
